newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures remained in a narrow range on Monday with traders preoccupied by a U.S. employment cost report due on Tuesday which was expected to give clues as to whether U.S. rates would be raised next month.
Traders said the session was relatively subdued with low volume and the slight decline in the U.S. bond market in the afternoon souring the early neutral tone.
"Everybody's waiting for tomorrow. As the (U.S.) bond wasn't too hot, we took the opportunity to take a breather," a trader said. He said the contract had closed at a zone of support at 130.14/16.
Traders said a quarter-on-quarter rise of more than 0.8 to 0.9 percent in the U.S. employment cost index would be enough to upset the bond market.
They said there was very little action in the cash market on Monday, although some said a few domestic investors had started looking to buy German bonds in a search for yield.
Analysts said the main domestic event this week would be the outcome of the Bank of France monetary policy council meeting, the second since two new members joined the policy setting body in January.
The Bank of France left its intervention rate unchanged at 3.15 percent after Monday's money market tender as expected.
The franc was little changed against the mark at 3.3712 compared with 3.3717 on Friday. It slipped against the dollar to 5.5364 from 5.4950.
Call money was unchanged at 3-3/16 5/16 percent.
